decision_conditions: Any development under Class A is permitted subject to the condition that it must be completed within a period of 3 years starting with the date prior approval is granted
Subject to the following conditions to secure matters, the proposal complies with the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (as amended) Schedule 2, Part 20, Class A.

Any development under Class A is permitted subject to the condition that before beginning the development, the developer must provide the local planning authority with a report for the management of the construction of the development, which sets out the proposed development hours of operation and how any adverse impact of noise, dust, vibration and traffic on occupiersof the building and adjoining owners or occupiers will be mitigated
The developer must notify the local planning authority of the completion of the development as soon as reasonably practicable after completion.
The notification referred to in sub-paragraph (3) must be in writing and must include—(a) the name of the developer;(b) the address or location of the development; and(c) the date of completion.

Any new dwellinghouse created under Class A is to remain in use as a dwellinghouse within the meaning of Class C3 of the Schedule to the Use Classes Order and for no other purpose, except to the extent that the other purpose is ancillary to the primary use as a dwellinghouse.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan2104	Proposed Third Floor Plan2105	Proposed Roof Plan2111 Proposed South-West Elevation2112 Proposed South-East Elevation2113 Proposed North-West Elevation2110 Proposed North-East Elevation2116 Proposed Section B-B2115 Proposed Section A-AReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture those specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area

Prior to occupation, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall be provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets

Prior to occupation, five long-stay cycle parking spaces shall be provided and unless otherwise agreed cycle parking should be provided in compliance with the following criteria:o	in an accessible location: the access route to the store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike too	enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) whicho	must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2mo	secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fobo	fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roofThe approved bicycle parking shall be provided prior to occupation and thereafter permanently retained. Reason: To ensure that sufficient provision at all times so that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or the conditions of general safety along the adjacent highway, or the amenities and convenience of existing local residents.
